ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE M.NAGAPRASANNA  ORAL ORDER

The petitioner is before this Court calling in question proceedings in C.C.No.50704/2019, pending before the XI ACMM at Bengaluru Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Bengaluru, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 504, 506 498A r/w. 34 of the IPC.

2. Heard Sri Supreeth S., learned counsel for the petitioner, Smt. Rashmi Patil, learned High Court Government NC: 2024:KHC:44523 Pleader for respondent No.1 and Sri Mohammed Rehaan Siddiq,
learned counsel for respondent No.2.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2 in unison submits that parties to the lis were before the family Court in M.C.No.3416/2019 and have settled their dispute amongst themselves before the mediation center.
The parties have decided to live together along with the child.
They have also appended a copy of the memorandum of settlement before this Court to that effect.

sentences.text:
The memorandum of settlement reads as follows:
"8.
Both the parties have forgiven and condoned each other for all their past acts and shall strive to live happily and harmoniously.

9. Both the parties have agreed to give space for each other and have agreed to respect their values, profession.
10.

In view of REUNION, the petitioner is no more interested in prosecuting C.C.No.50704/2019 pending on the file of XI ACMM, Bengaluru filed under Section 498-A, 506, 504 r/w 34 of IPC against the respondent herein and his family members, by cooperating and participating in seeking closure /quashing the said case in accordance with law.

11. Likewise, the respondent/husband has agreed to withdraw M.C.No.678/2019 pending on the file of VI Addl. Family Court, Bengaluru seeking decree of divorce against the petitioner/wife, as not pressed."

The offence alleged against the petitioner is under Section 506 of the IPC,
though it would not become the subject matter of settlement between the parties, since the dispute is between the husband and wife and the fact that the husband and wife have decided to live together, placing the afore-quoted terms and conditions of the memorandum of settlement on record, the impugned proceedings stand quashed.

5. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER a.
The criminal petition is disposed.
b. The proceedings in C.C.No.50704/2019, pending before the XI ACMM at Bengaluru Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Bengaluru, stand quashed.
c. It is needless to observe that the parties shall adhere to the terms and conditions of the settlement as quoted hereinabove.

Sd/-
(M.NAGAPRASANNA) JUDGE NVJ Sri Deva Kumar Stephen vs State Of Karnataka on 5 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17279593/
